releases.notes:
Find past workouts, pick up an unfinished review, and see your lifting records at a glance.

NEW
- Search completed workout sessions by workout or exercise, filter by date, and review every set.
- Repeat a session as an editable draft. Nothing is logged until you confirm.
- A simpler Progress overview highlights up to five top exercises with their weight personal records and dates. Open Details for goals, charts, reports, and more.
- Browse a larger collection of training quotes with a tap or swipe.

IMPROVED
- Resume interrupted workout reviews with your edited sets, notes, dates, exercise matches, and workout selections intact.
- More responsive typing and paste previews, plus smoother history loading.
- Clearer history text, set summaries, and date/time controls at larger text sizes.

FIXED
- Relative-date notes no longer split a workout into extra sessions, and unreadable pasted sections stay visible for review.
- If saved workouts cannot open, Marble preserves the original files and offers retry and recovery-copy options.
- Failed backup restores no longer leave partially restored changes behind.
- Progress quotes fit without shrinking or truncating, and swiping backward no longer also advances the quote.

Marble 2.4 makes adding a workout radically simpler.

NEW
- Add is now an AI-first workout composer: paste or type natural language, gym notation, multi-day Notes, or a Hevy or Strong CSV.
- Apple Intelligence structures prose on device when available; a deterministic parser handles notation and provides the fallback.
- Review every workout, exercise match, set, date, RPE, rest, and note before anything is saved.
- Drafts survive tab switches and relaunches, and Shortcuts can hand text directly to Add.

IMPROVED
- Strong exports handle European delimiters, decimal commas, kilograms, distance units, and supersets more accurately.
- Hevy imports preserve failed sets, RPE, notes, and session timing while skipping warmups.
- Weak exercise-name matches default to a new exercise instead of silently merging with the wrong movement.

Parsing and review stay on-device. Marble remains local-first: no account, no ads, no Marble server, and no third-party tracking.

Marble 2.3 makes it easier to train, log, and see progress without extra tabs.

NEW
- Train, Log, and Progress: Calendar and Supplements live inside Log. Planned sets with history complete in one tap.
- Typed and paste import: bring a Hevy, Strong, or Notes workout in as text, parse it on-device, and review every set before it is saved.
- Sprint V6: tenths-precision timing, a stopwatch, and more than one plan per sprint exercise.
- Editable weigh-ins: correct or delete a bodyweight entry so a typo does not stay in your progress.

IMPROVED
- Marble now runs on iOS 26.0, down from 26.2.
- Reliability fixes across backup restore, number entry, and system controls.

Marble remains local-first: no account, no ads, no Marble server, and no third-party tracking.

Marble 2.2 brings your training goals, quick logging, and progress beyond the app while keeping your data private.

NEW
- Weekly Goal widget for the Home Screen and Lock Screen, including quick log from the medium widget.
- Siri, Shortcuts, and Spotlight support for logging sets, repeating your last set, and starting or finishing workouts.
- Daily Highlights, a customizable private evening recap of truthful same-day progress.
- Bodyweight tracking with manual entry, Apple Health import, a bodyweight trend, and per-lift DOTS relative-strength scores.
- Three-step onboarding and a central Settings screen for units, weekly goals, reminders, Health options, backups, and privacy.
- Control Center, Lock Screen, and Action button access to quick logging.

IMPROVED
- Rest Live Activities now include +30 seconds and End controls, a rest-complete alert, and a clear stale state.
- JSON backup and restore now covers every persisted data type; photo and video files remain on your device.
- App Intents refresh widgets and reminders after logging, and restored data refreshes system surfaces immediately.
- Trends are faster on large histories and include accessible Audio Graph descriptions.
- Widgets support Smart Stack relevance, tinted rendering, and a dedicated privacy manifest.

Marble remains local-first: no account, no ads, no Marble server, and no third-party tracking.

Marble 2.1 makes it easier to plan a workout, stay in the flow, and keep your training history yours.

NEW
- Workout sessions: start, log, repeat, and finish a focused session while every set remains in your Journal.
- Sprint prescriptions: set distance, reps, a target time or range, and rest; each completed rep keeps the exact goal it was judged against.
- Exercise Library: search, favorite, create, and safely edit exercises from one redesigned home.
- Custom exercise icons: choose an emoji or SF Symbol for every movement.
- JSON backup and restore: move a complete local training record between devices without creating an account.

IMPROVED
- Weight-unit normalization keeps lb and kg comparisons accurate across history, records, and trends.
- Release-upgrade coverage now verifies the complete production model before launch.
- Data management explains exactly what is included in a backup and what stays on-device.

Marble remains private and local-first: no accounts, no ads, no tracking.

Marble 2.0 turns Trends into a coach. Everything is computed from your own logged sets, on your device.

NEW
- Your Lifts: estimated 1RM trend per lift with an honest verdict — progressing, holding, or adapted — compared at matched effort (RPE), so backing off never reads as stalling.
- Records: a feed of your genuine PRs in Trends, plus a quiet best-at-every-rep-count table for each exercise.
- PR in reach: while logging, Marble tells you when a weight or rep record is close enough to chase today.
- Double-progression hint: when every set tops 8 reps at the same load and manageable effort, Marble names the classic next step — with the evidence, never a command.
- Weekly Goal: set your sessions-per-week target and build a week streak that forgives — hit 4 weeks in a row to bank a flex week that absorbs a miss, and comebacks are celebrated.
- Monthly report: sessions, volume, and PRs with fair same-point-vs-last-month comparisons, plus short insights computed privately on your iPhone.
- Muscle groups now show weekly hard sets against the 10–20 set guide, count pressing/pulling assistance fractionally, and remind you when a muscle hasn't been trained lately.
- Send sessions to Apple Health (optional): completed training days export as strength workouts with your effort score, so Marble sessions count toward Apple's Training Load.

IMPROVED
- One quiet, adaptive weekly-goal reminder that cancels itself once you've trained.
- Best Weight comparisons are now unit-safe across lb and kg.

Marble remains local-only: no accounts, no ads, no tracking.

Marble 1.9 adds workout import, handwritten workout scanning, rest-timer Live Activities, and major performance polish.

NEW
- Import workouts from Apple Health, including Apple Watch and Garmin workouts that sync through Health.
- Scan handwritten workouts with on-device text recognition, review the parsed sets, then add them to your journal.
- Rest timer Live Activity and Dynamic Island support after logging sets with rest time.
- Clearer Import hub with Garmin-via-Health guidance and privacy-first source labeling.

IMPROVED
- Faster Journal, Calendar, and Trends screens with memoized chart and list data.
- Refined Trends summary with sets, best week, supplements, charts, PRs, and drill-downs.
- Better first-run Journal checklist, smoother Add Set flow, and Save + Next logging.
- iOS 26 visual polish, updated symbols, and more reliable widget packaging.

Marble remains local-only: no accounts, no ads, no tracking.

Marble 1.8 is a big quality release: faster everywhere, smarter with long training histories, and better integrated with iOS.

NEW
• Custom reminders: schedule weekly notifications for training days, supplements, or anything else you want to stay on top of.
• Siri & Shortcuts: say "Log a set in Marble" or trigger "Log Last Set Again" from Shortcuts, Spotlight, or the Action button.
• Smarter long-range Trends: 1-year and all-time charts now aggregate by week, with week-by-week drill-downs into your sets and supplement logs.

IMPROVED
• Major performance work across Journal, Calendar, and Trends — scrolling and chart scrubbing stay smooth even with years of logged sets.
• Refined iOS 26 design with native Liquid Glass navigation, and the tab bar now tucks away while you scroll your log.
• Haptic feedback confirms saving, repeating, and deleting sets.
• Shake-to-undo works alongside the existing Undo buttons.
• Better Dynamic Type support: icons scale with your text size and labels no longer clip at accessibility sizes.
• "Today" and "Yesterday" labels stay correct when the app returns from the background on a new day.
• Trends exercise filtering with search, recents, and per-exercise best lifts.

FIXED
• Duplicating a set (or undoing a delete) now keeps its distance values.
• Failed saves roll back cleanly and let you know, instead of failing silently.

No accounts. No ads. No tracking. Your training stays on your device.
New in 1.7: Add custom supplement reminders with multiple times, weekday schedules, and confirmation before logging. Also includes reliability and UI test improvements.

New in 1.6:
- Attach progress photos and videos to calendar dates to track physique changes alongside training.
- Refreshed key screens to better follow iOS navigation, spacing, contrast, and accessibility patterns.
- Improved Trends and Calendar coverage for a smoother, more reliable logging experience.
Search exercise titles to more easily add new sets

- see what weight + reps for your previous set whenever logging a new one
